safeguarding.blocked: I can't answer that here. If something is weighing on you or someone is hurting you, please talk to an adult you trust – or call Childline on 0800 1111 (free and confidential). I'm still here for you.
safeguarding.concern: Thank you for telling me – that matters, and you're not alone with it. Please talk to an adult you trust. You can also call Childline on 0800 1111 (free and confidential, you don't have to give your name). I'm still here for you.
safeguarding.blocked_adult: I can't answer that here. If something is weighing on you, please talk to someone you trust. If you are in danger, call the emergency number 112.
safeguarding.concern_adult: Thank you for telling me – that matters. Please talk to someone you trust. If you are in danger, call the emergency number 112. I'm still here for you.
safeguarding.also_asked: I haven't forgotten what you asked about your learning – just tell me when you want us to look at it together.
safeguarding.also_asked_adult: I haven't forgotten what you asked about your learning – tell me when you want to look at it.
safeguarding.held_back: (A message the safety filter held back.)

push.idea: Buddy has an idea for you.
push.checkin: Buddy would like to check in.
push.result: Buddy has something ready for you.

reminder.late: I meant to remind you at {{time}} – sorry, this comes late. {{text}}
reminder.checkin_unavailable: I wanted to check in with you, but I can't quite get to it right now. Just write to me if you like.
reminder.practice_ready: As agreed: {{title}}. {{count}} questions are ready, about {{minutes}} minutes.
reminder.practice_ready_one: As agreed: {{title}}. One question is ready, about {{minutes}} minutes.
reminder.capture: As agreed: {{title}} – a photo is enough, I'll do the rest.

exam.prepared: {{day}} is “{{exam}}”. {{count}} questions are ready, about {{minutes}} minutes.
exam.prepared_one: {{day}} is “{{exam}}”. One question is ready, about {{minutes}} minutes.
exam.need_material: {{day}} is “{{exam}}”. Do you have a worksheet for it? A photo is enough, I'll do the rest.
exam.followup: How did “{{exam}}” go? Tell me briefly and I'll plan the next steps.

bar.add_prompt: Work out {{first}} + {{second}} and shade in the result.
bar.hint_parts: The bar is divided into {{parts}} equal parts.
bar.hint_shade: How many of those parts are {{fraction}}?
bar.hint_compare_reach: Look at how far the shaded part reaches in each bar.
bar.hint_compare_parts: The more parts a whole has, the smaller one part is.
bar.hint_add_same: Both fractions are divided into equal parts here.
bar.hint_add_count: Count the shaded parts of both bars together.
bar.worked_shade: The whole bar is {{parts}} parts. {{fraction}} of it is {{answer}}.
bar.worked_compare: {{answer}} reaches further in the bar – that is the bigger fraction.
bar.worked_add: Both fractions are divided into {{parts}} equal parts. Together {{answer}} is shaded.

practice.cannot_check: I can't check that right now. You can look at the solution and compare yourself.
practice.had_enough: Okay — that is enough for today if you want. You can end the practice, or we do one small example together. Just say which you would rather.
practice.heard_retry: I couldn't hear you well. Try again a bit louder and closer to the phone.
practice.help_final_answer: That looks good! Now write down your final result – the way the task asks for it.
practice.help_step: Let's go step by step: what does the task give you, and what are you looking for?
practice.missing_word: Almost – a word is still missing. Take another look.
practice.no_single_solution: There isn't one right answer I could show you here: in a text like this, what counts is how you argue it. Tell me where you're stuck and we'll look at your text together.
practice.not_lowest: Balanced correctly! Now reduce it – every number in front divides by {{factor}}.
practice.not_quite: Not quite yet. Have another look at the question – or show the solution.
practice.not_transformed: Equivalent – but that's exactly how the task already writes it. Transform it a bit further.
practice.one_way_intro: Here's one way to go about it – one way, not the only one:

rubric.next_judged: That part holds. Have another look at whether {{name}} is in there: {{missing}}
rubric.next_verb: That part holds. Only at “{{verb}}” the tense isn’t right yet: {{missing}}

practice.speak_almost: Almost! Look at the marked words.
practice.speak_retry: Try again – listen to it first.
practice.spelling: Almost right – look closely at capital letters and punctuation.

staff.interval_prompt: Which interval lies between the two notes?
staff.time_prompt: Which time signature is this line in?
staff.hint_note_clef: The {{clef}} fixes one line – from there you count on: line, space, line.
staff.hint_note_step: Is the note on a line or in a space?
staff.hint_value_head: Look at the note head: is it filled in, and does it have a stem?
staff.hint_value_rest: A rest lasts as long as the note it replaces.
staff.hint_value_flag: Every flag on the stem halves the value.
staff.hint_value_dot: A dot after it makes the symbol half as long again.
staff.hint_interval_count: Count the steps from the lower note up to the higher one – the lower one is 1.
staff.hint_interval_quality: Then count the semitones: they decide whether the step is perfect, major or minor.
staff.hint_time_add: Add up the values in one bar.
staff.hint_time_unit: The lower number says which note value gets one beat, the upper one how many of those go into a bar.
staff.hint_write_clef: Start with the first note – the {{clef}} tells you which line it sits on.
staff.hint_write_fill: A bar is only finished when its values together fill the whole bar.
staff.worked_note: Counted out in the {{clef}} from the line the clef fixes, this note comes out as {{answer}}.
staff.worked_value: Head, stem and flag together tell you the value: {{answer}}.
staff.worked_interval: From {{lower}} to {{upper}} it is {{steps}} steps. With the semitones in between that makes {{answer}}.
staff.worked_time: Add up the values of one bar: they fill exactly one bar of {{answer}}.
staff.worked_write: This is what the line looks like: {{answer}}. Every bar is full when its values together make one bar of {{time}}.
staff.again_note: Not quite yet. In the {{clef}}, count from the line the clef fixes.
staff.again_value: Not quite yet. Have another look at the head, the stem and the flag.
staff.again_interval: Not quite yet. Count the steps along – the lower note is 1.
staff.again_time: Not quite yet. Add up the values of one bar.
staff.again_write: Not quite yet. Have another look at your line, symbol by symbol.
staff.held: The first {{held}} of {{total}} symbols are right.
staff.held_one: The first of {{total}} symbols is right.
staff.fault_too_many: You have put in one symbol too many.
staff.fault_bar_over: Bar {{bar}} holds more than fits into the bar.
staff.fault_bar_under: Bar {{bar}} still needs something to make the bar full.
staff.fault_pitch: Symbol number {{index}} in bar {{bar}} isn't on the right line yet.
staff.fault_value: Symbol number {{index}} in bar {{bar}} still has the wrong value.
staff.fault_rest_here: Position number {{index}} in bar {{bar}} needs a rest.
staff.fault_note_here: Position number {{index}} in bar {{bar}} needs a note.

practice.same_value: The value is right – you've just written it differently. Check which form the task wants the result in.
practice.step_broke: Everything holds up to line {{line}}. Something gets lost on the way to the next line – take another look at that step.
practice.step_broke_last: Your way is right all the way through – only the last step is not. Take another look at the last line.
practice.test_no_hints: There are no hints in a test – just write what you think, or skip the question.
practice.test_noted: Noted – on to the next one.
practice.try_again: Not quite yet – have another go. Tap “Hint” for a clue.
practice.typo: Almost – it's spelled {{answer}}. Type it once more.
practice.typo_extra: Almost – there's one letter too many. Take another close look.
practice.typo_missing: Almost – there's a letter missing. Take another close look.
practice.typo_swapped: Almost – two letters are the wrong way round. Can you spot them?
practice.typo_wrong: Almost – one letter isn't right yet. Can you spot it?
practice.unbalanced_charge: Almost – the charges don't match yet: {{left}} on the left, {{right}} on the right.
practice.unbalanced_element: Almost – count the {{element}} again: {{left}} on the left, {{right}} on the right.
practice.unbalanced_mass: Almost – the mass numbers don't match yet: {{left}} on the left, {{right}} on the right.
practice.unbalanced_atomic: Almost – the atomic numbers don't match yet: {{left}} on the left, {{right}} on the right.

order.first_wrong: Not quite yet – have another look at what comes first.
order.right_until: Right up to step {{right}}! From step {{from}} on, the order isn't quite there yet.

table.near_one: Only a tiny detail is missing at {{cell}}.
table.look_more: Have another look at {{cells}} and {{more}} more.
table.none_right: None of the cells is right yet – best start with {{cell}}.
table.near_many: Only a tiny detail is missing at {{cells}}.
table.near_more: Only a tiny detail is missing at {{cells}} and {{more}} more.

match.pairs_none: None of the pairs fits yet – take another calm look.
match.groups_some: {{count}} of {{total}} are already in the right group.
match.groups_some_one: 1 of {{total}} is already in the right group.
match.groups_none: None is in the right group yet – take another calm look.

figure.x_right: The x-coordinate is right already – look again at how far up or down it goes.
figure.y_right: The y-coordinate is right already – look again at how far right or left it goes.
figure.swapped: Nearly – you swapped x and y. First go right or left, then up or down.
figure.point_wrong: Not the right point yet – go right or left first, then up or down.
figure.place_wrong: Not the right spot yet – count the steps between the marks again.
figure.further_right: The spot you are looking for is further to the right.
figure.further_left: The spot you are looking for is further to the left.
figure.bar_wrong: Not this bar yet – compare the heights again calmly.
figure.hour_right: The hour is right already – look again at the long hand.
figure.minute_right: The minutes are right already – look again at the short hand.
figure.time_wrong: Not the right time yet – set the short hand first, then the long one.
figure.group_right: That is {{tapped}} — the group is right. Look in another period.
figure.period_right: That is {{tapped}} — the period is right. Look in another group.
figure.element_wrong: That is {{tapped}}. Another element is wanted.
figure.part_wrong: That is: {{tapped}}. Another part is wanted.
figure.color_wrong: That is {{tapped}}. Have another look at the wheel.
figure.lamp_wrong: Not this lamp. Follow the current from the plus pole.

draw.line_solution: The line y = {{fn}}, for example through {{points}}
draw.point_wrong: Take another look at the point {{point}}.
draw.line_slope_right: The slope is right already – but the line crosses the y-axis at the wrong place.
draw.line_intercept_right: The line already crosses the y-axis at the right place – the slope is not right yet.
draw.line_point_off: The point {{point}} is not on the line yet.
draw.line_vertical: Your two points are exactly above each other – take two places side by side.
draw.same_x: Two of your points have the same x-coordinate – take different places.
draw.graph_point_off: The point {{point}} is not on the graph yet.
draw.cells_missing_one: Nearly – one square is still missing.
draw.cells_extra: Nearly – {{count}} squares too many are coloured.
draw.cells_extra_one: Nearly – one square too many is coloured.
draw.cells_both: Not quite yet – squares are missing ({{missing}}) and some are coloured too many ({{extra}}).
draw.bar_wrong: The bar “{{label}}” is not at the right height yet.

library.el_find: Tap the element {{name}} in the periodic table.
library.el_protons: How many protons does an atom of {{name}} ({{sym}}) have?
library.el_electrons: How many electrons does a neutral atom of {{name}} ({{sym}}) have?
library.el_neutrons: An atom of {{name}} has the atomic mass {{mass}} u. How many neutrons does it have? Round the mass to a whole number.
library.el_valence: How many valence electrons does an atom of {{name}} have?
library.el_class: Is {{name}} a metal, a metalloid or a nonmetal?
library.el_more_en: Which of the two elements has the higher electronegativity?
library.hint_find: The symbol of this element is {{sym}}.
library.hint_locate: The periods are the rows, the groups the columns.
library.hint_z: The number in the box is the atomic number.
library.hint_electrons: Neutral means: as many electrons as protons.
library.hint_valence: For main-group elements, the number of the main group tells you how many.
library.hint_group: The main groups are the columns, I to VIII.
library.hint_period: Count the rows from the top.
library.hint_class: Metals are on the left and at the bottom, nonmetals at the top right, metalloids on the staircase between them.
library.hint_en: Electronegativity increases to the right and upwards.
library.worked_protons: {{name}} has the atomic number {{z}}, so {{z}} protons.
library.worked_electrons: {{name}} has {{z}} protons; a neutral atom has just as many electrons: {{z}}.
library.worked_neutrons: {{mass}} u rounded is {{rounded}}. The atomic number is {{z}}. {{rounded}} − {{z}} = {{n}} neutrons.
library.worked_valence: {{name}} is in main group {{group}}, so it has {{v}} valence electrons.
library.worked_period: {{name}} is in row {{period}}, so in period {{period}}.
library.part_match: Which name goes with which number?
library.hint_part: Each dot at the edge belongs to the part its line points to.
library.hint_part_name: Follow the line from the number to its part.
library.c_dark: One lamp does not light. Tap it.
library.c_lit: Only one lamp lights. Tap it.
library.c_connection: How are the lamps and resistors connected here?
library.c_resistance: What is the equivalent resistance of the whole circuit?
library.hint_path: Follow the current from plus to minus. Where a switch is open, it stops.
library.hint_connection: In series the current has one path, in parallel several paths side by side.
library.hint_resistance: In series the resistances add up. In parallel: 1/R = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂.
library.hint_current: First work out the equivalent resistance, then I = U / R.
library.hint_voltage: Work out the current through the part, then U = R · I.
library.worked_dark: No current flows through {{lamp}}, so it stays dark.
library.worked_conn_series: All parts are one after another on one path: a series circuit.
library.worked_conn_parallel: Each part has its own branch: a parallel circuit.
library.worked_conn_mixed: Some parts are in series, some in parallel: a mixed circuit.
library.worked_voltage: The voltage across the part is {{value}} {{unit}}.
library.hint_gate_and: & (AND) gives 1 only when both inputs are 1.
library.hint_gate_or: ≥1 (OR) gives 1 as soon as at least one input is 1.
library.hint_gate_xor: =1 (XOR) gives 1 when exactly one input is 1.
library.hint_gate_nand: The circle at the output inverts the result: NAND is AND, inverted.
library.hint_gate_nor: The circle at the output inverts the result: NOR is OR, inverted.
library.col_mix: Which colour do {{a}} and {{b}} make? Tap it.
library.hint_col_complement: The complementary colour lies exactly opposite in the wheel.
library.hint_col_mix: The mixed colour lies between the two colours in the wheel.
library.worked_col_find: {{key}} is the field with that name.

contact.less_often: Got it – from now on I'll only message your phone when it really matters. Everything else waits here. You can change this in settings.
